definition: A decoding strategy that restricts sampling to the k most probable next tokens at each step, discarding the rest of the distribution.
details: Top-k sampling balances diversity and quality by preventing the model from sampling extremely unlikely (and often nonsensical) tokens while still allowing some randomness.

explainer.lead: Top-k sampling restricts generation to the k most probable next tokens, discarding the rest of the distribution. It matters because it blocks nonsensical picks while keeping some randomness.

tiers.eli5: You let the model choose only from its k favourite next words, so it can still surprise you but not go off the rails.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers set k to balance diversity and quality per task. A pitfall is a fixed k: it truncates too much on flat distributions and too little on sharp ones.
tiers.paperLevel: At each step, sample from the k highest-probability tokens only; the rest are discarded. Limits: k is static, so it does not adapt to the shape of the distribution.

explainer.example: With k=10, a model that would otherwise pick an odd rare word can only choose among its 10 most likely candidates.
